claims.claim_ar: دعاء بصيغة أمرية متضمّن تضرعاً وخفيةً في قول يوسف: «رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي...»، أي طلب بتضعّف وخشية.
claims.claim_en: A supplicatory imperative expressed with humility and secrecy in Yusuf's plea 'My Lord, forgive me...', i.e. a petition marked by humble entreaty.

claims.claim_ar: التوازي والتراكم في الطلبات عبر ربط الواو العاطفة: «اغفر لي ولأخي وأدخلنا…»، حيث توالي الطلبات يضاعف الإلحاح البلاغي.
claims.claim_en: Parallelism/accumulation of petitions through the copulative waw: 'forgive me and my brother and admit us...', where the successive requests increase rhetorical urgency.
claims.needs_review_reason: Classifying simple coordination as 'm uqabalah' (مقابلة/مقابلة شبيهة بالموازنة) may be debatable; could be described simply as coordination/parallelism.

claims.claim_ar: الانتقال إلى الكلام المباشر (افتتاح الصيغة بـ«قَالَ رَبِّ…»)، شكل من أشكال الالتفات البلاغي الذي يقوّي حضور المتكلّم في النص.
claims.claim_en: The shift to direct speech (opening with 'He said, My Lord...') is an iltifat — a rhetorical turn that strengthens the speaker's presence.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source quoted discusses 'قوله' and its interpretation but does not explicitly use the technical term 'iltifat'; the identification is an interpretive inference.

warnings: Requested balagha sources (al-Jurjani, al-Sakkaki, al-Baqillani, al-Suyuti, and a tafsir-balagha section) are not present among the provided source_chunks. Claims above are supported by the available chunks (e.g., Zamakhshari, Tabari, Darwish, Safi) and include some interpretive inferences.
Some device labels (e.g., classifying coordination as 'm uqabalah' or identifying 'iltifat') are interpretive and flagged in 'needs_review_reason' where appropriate.
